sourcePolicy: Official ISM monthly reports are authoritative. This file stores a compact analytical snapshot and selected Power Stack-relevant observations, not a reconstructed ISM index database or confidential survey submissions.

industryRead.notableDetail: Electrical Equipment and Computer & Electronic Products reported higher new orders; both also reported higher prices, slower supplier deliveries and customers' inventories that were too low. Computer & Electronic Products also reported higher production, employment and backlog.

manufacturing.powerStackInterpretation: Manufacturing orders, production, employment and backlog strengthened while customer inventories stayed too low. Electrical/electronic growth plus component scarcity supports pricing power for equipment suppliers; high prices and slower deliveries remain execution risks for contractors.

industryRead.commentRead: Construction remained in expansion and reported higher new orders and employment, while public commentary and prices data continue to show cost pressure.

services.powerStackInterpretation: Services demand remains resilient but expensive. Business Activity and New Orders accelerated while Prices exceeded 70 and employment contracted. Switchgear, transformers, wire/cable and technical labour remain direct infrastructure bottlenecks.

respondentCommentReview.scope: Only ISM-selected public respondent comments and aggregate diffusion data were reviewed.
respondentCommentReview.finding: Re-verified Aug 27. July remains the latest official Manufacturing and Services dataset. The public July manufacturing roundup explicitly notes the AI boom/data-centre buildup as an uncertainty alongside Iran/product availability and tariffs. Aggregate evidence still shows Electrical Equipment and Computer & Electronic Products expanding with too-low customer inventories and scarcity in memory/semiconductors/electrical components; services separately flags switchgear/transformer/wire-cable pressure.
respondentCommentReview.conclusion: Official July evidence reinforces physical bottlenecks but does not justify claims about confidential respondents, named hyperscalers or individual data-centre projects.

combinedRead: July ISM remains constructive for Power Stack physical demand but not cleanly disinflationary: manufacturing re-accelerated and services demand stayed firm while prices, supplier delays and scarce electrical/electronic inputs remained elevated. Prefer backlog-rich equipment, generation, grid, cable and first-wave automation suppliers with pricing power over low-margin contractors and long-duration concept equities.
rawSubmissionNote: ISM does not publish the confidential individual survey submission database. Only aggregate diffusion data and selected respondent comments are public; Power Stack does not claim access to raw panel submissions.
